title: Finite coefficient compatibility of exceptional composition
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [sk-def-sf-setting]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-morphisms; put $x=g\circ f$. Use the constructible finite-Tor categories $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ and the specified operations of [sk-def-sf-operations], with derived-complete integral, raw rationalized and common-finite-stage coefficients. Write $F_{h,\Lambda}=Rh_{!,\Lambda}$, $G_{h,\Lambda}=Rh^!_\Lambda$ and $\epsilon_{h,\Lambda}$ for the counits of their constructible adjunctions $F_{h,\Lambda}\dashv G_{h,\Lambda}$ at every stage [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients], for $h=f,g,x$. For a finite extension $E\subset E'$ the same notation at the target coefficient stages uses $E'$ in place of $E$, as in that node.

Write $\alpha_\Lambda:F_{g,\Lambda}F_{f,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{x,\Lambda}$ for the canonical compactification compositor: at finite level the composition isomorphism of [thm-sf-comp-composition], restricted to the finite-Tor constructible categories, and at the integral, rational and common stages its completed integral form and its rationalized/common-stage forms. Let $c_\Lambda:G_{f,\Lambda}G_{g,\Lambda}\to G_{x,\Lambda}$ denote the conjugate of $\alpha_\Lambda^{-1}$ under the composite adjunction and $F_{x,\Lambda}\dashv G_{x,\Lambda}$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate].

Consider a finite quotient $A=A_n\to B=A_m$ with $1\le m\le n$, or a finite-free change $A=A_n\to B=R'/\varpi^nR'$ where $E\subset E'$ is finite and $R'=\mathcal O_{E'}$, and any subsequent positive quotient of this $B$. Write $C_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$. For each $h:U\to V$ among $f,g,x$ let $q_h:C_VF_{h,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h,B}C_U$ be the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison and $b_h:C_UG_{h,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,B}C_V$ its counit-normalized exceptional comparison of [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients], that is the transpose of $C_V(\epsilon_{h,A})\circ q_{h,G_{h,A}}^{-1}$. Put $q_{g,f}=(F_{g,B}q_f)\circ(q_gF_{f,A})$.

The exceptional composition comparisons satisfy
$$b_{x,L}\circ C_X(c_{A,L})=c_{B,C_ZL}\circ G_{f,B}(b_{g,L})\circ b_{f,G_{g,A}L}\qquad(L\in\mathcal C_{Z,A}).$$
More precisely, if $U_L=G_{f,A}G_{g,A}L$ and $\beta_{A,L}=\epsilon_{g,A,L}\circ F_{g,A}(\epsilon_{f,A,G_{g,A}L})$, both sides of this equation have the same $F_{x,B}\dashv G_{x,B}$ transpose
$$C_Z(\beta_{A,L})\circ q_{g,f,U_L}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{B,C_XU_L}^{-1}:F_{x,B}C_XU_L\longrightarrow C_ZL.$$
This is an equality of natural transformations on the finite-Tor constructible domains, using the specified compactification maps on the small pro-etale sites. They include ramified extensions: if $e=e(E'/E)$, then $R'/\varpi^nR'=A_{E',en}$ under $(\varpi^n)=(\varpi_{E'}^{en})$. No flatness of the finite quotient is assumed.

proof.text:
Fix $L$ and abbreviate $V=G_{g,A}L$, $U=G_{f,A}V$. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] the counit for $F_{g,A}F_{f,A}\dashv G_{f,A}G_{g,A}$ is $\beta_{A,L}=\epsilon_{g,A,L}\circ F_{g,A}(\epsilon_{f,A,V})$. The definition of conjugation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], together with the transpose characterization [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], says that the transpose of $c_{A,L}$ is $\beta_{A,L}\circ\alpha_{A,U}^{-1}$. Consequently
$$\epsilon_{x,A,L}\circ F_{x,A}(c_{A,L})=\beta_{A,L}\circ\alpha_{A,U}^{-1}.$$
The identical formula holds at $B$. These formulas use the given adjunctions, not an ambient exceptional-adjoint datum.

source.place: Final compatibility sentence, expanded by the worker into the left coefficient square and two explicit counit transposes

proof.text:
Let $a=b_{x,L}\circ C_X(c_{A,L})$. Its $F_{x,B}\dashv G_{x,B}$ transpose is $\epsilon_{x,B,C_ZL}\circ F_{x,B}(a)$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The counit equation of [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients] for $x$, followed by naturality of $q_x^{-1}$ at $c_{A,L}$, gives
$$a^\flat=C_Z(\epsilon_{x,A,L})\circ q_{x,G_{x,A}L}^{-1}\circ F_{x,B}C_X(c_{A,L})
=C_Z(\epsilon_{x,A,L}\circ F_{x,A}(c_{A,L}))\circ q_{x,U}^{-1}.$$
Use step 2, then the inverse form of the square in step 1,
$$C_Z(\alpha_{A,U}^{-1})\circ q_{x,U}^{-1}=q_{g,f,U}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{B,C_XU}^{-1},$$
to obtain $a^\flat=C_Z(\beta_{A,L})\circ q_{g,f,U}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{B,C_XU}^{-1}$, exactly the displayed transpose in the statement.

source.place: Final compatibility sentence, expanded by the worker into the left coefficient square and two explicit counit transposes

proof.text:
Put $r=G_{f,B}(b_{g,L})\circ b_{f,V}$ and $d=c_{B,C_ZL}\circ r$. By step 2 at $B$ and naturality of $\alpha_B^{-1}$, its transpose is
$$d^\flat=\beta_{B,C_ZL}\circ F_{g,B}F_{f,B}(r)\circ\alpha_{B,C_XU}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $\epsilon_{f,B}$ at $b_{g,L}:C_YV\to G_{g,B}C_ZL$ changes the factor before $\alpha_B^{-1}$ to
$$\epsilon_{g,B,C_ZL}\circ F_{g,B}(b_{g,L})\circ F_{g,B}(\epsilon_{f,B,C_YV}\circ F_{f,B}(b_{f,V})).$$
Apply the counit equations of [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients] first for $f$ and then for $g$. This factor becomes
$$C_Z(\epsilon_{g,A,L})\circ q_{g,V}^{-1}\circ F_{g,B}C_Y(\epsilon_{f,A,V})\circ F_{g,B}(q_{f,U}^{-1}).$$
Naturality of $q_g^{-1}$ at $\epsilon_{f,A,V}:F_{f,A}U\to V$ makes it
$$C_Z(\epsilon_{g,A,L}\circ F_{g,A}(\epsilon_{f,A,V}))\circ q_{g,F_{f,A}U}^{-1}\circ F_{g,B}(q_{f,U}^{-1})=C_Z(\beta_{A,L})\circ q_{g,f,U}^{-1}.$$
Appending $\alpha_{B,C_XU}^{-1}$ therefore gives the same transpose as step 3. This is just counit naturality and the two given counit equations; no coefficient/exceptional composition compatibility has been presumed.

proof.text: The transposition map is injective, since it is the inverse of the adjunction Hom bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The equality of the transposes computed in steps 3 and 4 gives $a=d$, the required equation. All constituent maps are natural transformations on the stated constructible categories, so the component equality for every $L$ is their equality as natural transformations. The quotient argument never invokes exact underived scalar extension; all coefficient functors are derived tensor. In particular the argument includes $m=n$, identity geometric morphisms, zero complexes, and the ramified level $en$ followed by any positive quotient.
